pois.name: Senso-ji Temple
pois.description: Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Gate into Tokyo's oldest and most sacred Buddhist temple.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Best visited in the morning before crowds arrive
✓ Free historic cultural site
✓ 4.7★ reviews
pois.tip: Visit before 9:00 AM for quiet photo opportunities.

pois.name: Tokyo Skytree
pois.description: Ascend 350 meters above ground to panoramic glass observation decks.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Iconic 360-degree panoramic skyline views
✓ High photo spot rating
pois.tip: Pre-book tickets online to skip entrance lines.

pois.name: Ichiran Ramen Asakusa
pois.description: Savor world-famous tonkotsu ramen served in private solo dining booths.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ 350m walk from Senso-ji Temple
✓ High rating for authentic Japanese ramen
pois.tip: Use the ticket vending machine at the entrance.

pois.name: Tokyo National Museum
pois.description: Explore Japan's oldest and largest art museum holding samurai armor and national treasures.
pois.ai_reason: ✓ Premier cultural institution in Ueno Park
pois.tip: Check the Japanese Gallery (Honkan) first.
nearby: National Museum of Nature and Science

pois.name: Shibuya Sky
pois.description: Stand on an open-air rooftop sky deck 229 meters above Shibuya Crossing.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Top-rated sunset spot (4.8★)
✓ Panoramic open-air glass rooftop
pois.tip: Book sunset time slots at least 2 weeks in advance.

pois.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
pois.description: Shinto shrine dedicated to the deified spirits of Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken surrounded by serene cedar forest.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Iconic tranquil cedar forest in central Tokyo
✓ Free historic cultural site
pois.tip: Walk through the giant cypress Torii gates early in the morning for peaceful contemplation.

pois.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
pois.description: Sprawling landscaped park blending traditional Japanese, English Landscape, and French Formal gardens.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Picturesque walking paths and scenic greenhouse
✓ Tranquil natural retreat
pois.tip: Visit the traditional Japanese Landscape Garden tea house for matcha.

pois.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
pois.description: Bustling marketplace with wholesale food stalls, fresh seafood, tamagoyaki, and Japanese culinary street snacks.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Unmatched street food and culinary tasting promenade
✓ Historic morning market culture
pois.tip: Arrive hungry between 8:30 AM and 11:00 AM for fresh seasonal specialties.

pois.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
pois.description: Historic castle grounds of former Edo Castle featuring stone ramparts, Ninomaru Garden, and ancient moats.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Free imperial heritage site
✓ Historic samurai fortress grounds
pois.tip: Walk up to the stone foundation of the former castle keep for panoramic garden views.

pois.name: Ueno Park & Shinobazu Pond
pois.description: Iconic public cultural park home to lotus ponds, shrines, museums, and scenic tree-lined boulevards.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Premier cultural public park in Tokyo
✓ High family suitability rating
pois.tip: Rent a swan paddle boat on Shinobazu Pond in the afternoon.

pois.name: Akihabara Electric Town
pois.description: World-famous technology, gaming, anime, and electronics capital glowing with neon facades and multi-story hobby shops.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Center of Japanese pop culture and electronics
✓ Vibrant neon atmosphere
pois.tip: Main Chuo-dori street becomes a pedestrian paradise on Sunday afternoons.

pois.name: teamLab Planets Toyosu
pois.description: Immersive digital art museum where visitors walk barefoot through knee-deep water and infinite crystal light installations.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ World-acclaimed interactive digital art experience
✓ Unmatched sensory photo opportunities
pois.tip: Wear pants that can be rolled up past knees as some exhibits involve wading in water.

pois.name: Tokyo Tower
pois.description: Iconic Eiffel-inspired communications tower rising 333 meters over Shiba Park with glass-floor observation platforms.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Classic retro symbol of modern Tokyo
✓ Spectacular night illuminations
pois.tip: Visit at dusk to watch the orange lattice tower light up against the Tokyo skyline.

pois.name: Hamarikyu Gardens
pois.description: Seaside tidal garden of the Tokugawa Shoguns featuring a serene teahouse on a tidal pond framed by Shiodome skyscrapers.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Peaceful tranquil contrast between historic Edo garden and modern towers
✓ Low crowd rating
pois.tip: Order matcha and seasonal wagashi sweet at the Nakajima Teahouse overlooking the pond.

pois.name: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower Sky Deck
pois.description: Observation facility on the 52nd floor with direct sightlines to Tokyo Tower and contemporary Mori Art Museum exhibitions.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Best vantage point for photographing Tokyo Tower lit up at night
✓ Includes Mori Art Museum entry
pois.tip: Pair observation deck with the world-class modern art exhibitions at Mori Art Museum.

pois.name: Harajuku Takeshita Street
pois.description: Pedestrian shopping hub of Japanese youth culture, quirky fashion boutiques, crepe stands, and colorful character cafes.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Vibrant center of Harajuku youth subcultures
✓ Family and teen entertainment hub
pois.tip: Try a fresh Marion Crepe while browsing the vibrant boutique alleys.

pois.name: Nezu Shrine
pois.description: One of Tokyo's oldest Shinto shrines featuring a picturesque tunnel of vermilion torii gates and tranquil koi ponds.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Authentic hidden gem away from dense tourist crowds
✓ Red torii gate tunnel similar to Kyoto Fushimi Inari
pois.tip: Stroll through the hillside azalea sanctuary and vermilion torii tunnel in peaceful seclusion.

pois.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck
pois.description: Twin municipal skyscraper towers with completely free panoramic 45th-floor observation floors offering vistas to Mount Fuji.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Free 202-meter high observation deck with panoramic Mount Fuji vistas
✓ Top value budget highlight
pois.tip: Visit on crisp clear winter mornings for the highest chance of seeing Mount Fuji.

pois.name: Afuri Ramen Harajuku
pois.description: Acclaimed ramen parlor famous for light, refreshing yuzu citrus broth and charcoal-grilled chashu pork.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Acclaimed yuzu shio ramen broth
✓ Conveniently located near Harajuku Station
pois.tip: Order the signature Yuzu Shio Ramen and customize chicken oil level to 'Tanrei'.

pois.name: Koishikawa Korakuen Garden
pois.description: One of Tokyo's oldest and best preserved Edo-period circuit stroll gardens featuring Chinese landscaping themes.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Authentic peaceful strolling garden with stone bridges and weeping cherry trees
✓ Low crowd rating
pois.tip: Cross the Full Moon Stone Bridge and admire the Engetsu-kyo reflection in the pond.

pois.name: Ginza Kagari Soba & Ramen
pois.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand recognized ramen sanctuary acclaimed for velvety rich tori paitan chicken broth.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Acclaimed gourmet chicken paitan ramen
✓ Located in prestigious Ginza quarter
pois.tip: Add a seasoned soft-boiled egg and seasonal vegetable toppings.

pois.name: Kanda Myojin Shrine
pois.description: Historic 1,300-year-old Shinto shrine honoring the guardian deity of Tokyo and popular for tech talisman blessings.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ 1,300 years of Tokyo history
✓ Beautiful lacquered shrine gate and cultural hall
pois.tip: Browse the unique electronics and IT safety amulets available at the shrine shop.

pois.name: Omoide Yokocho
pois.description: Atmospheric post-war alleyway packed with tiny charcoal yakitori stalls, lanterns, and nostalgic Showa-era charm.
pois.ai_reason:
✓ Quintessential retro Showa alleyway dining atmosphere
✓ Fresh charcoal yakitori skewers
pois.tip: Take a counter seat at a yakitori stall and order negima chicken and cold draft beer.
